account:
Today appears fairly quiet from what I have directly learned. I attended the market walk, returned home for lunch, and came back for the one o'clock accounts appointment. The builder requested a paid repair commission this morning, including clear work locations, standards, and a budget. I asked for a bridge safety inspection and itemized estimate, but authorized no construction or payment. I have not yet received an estimate.

Several townspeople have repeated reports of the baker carrying bread at the inn and plaza, and wheat at the bakery. The baker told me thirty-two fresh loaves were stocked at the market and reported no town problem. I saw bread being put in the stall chest and bought two loaves. Those movements may simply be normal baking and selling; I have no evidence of a special gathering or anything improper.

The afternoon tea appointment initially lacked a host name and precise address. The secretary now says the neighbour confirmed three o'clock tea at the east-bank cottage at (16, -60, 105), with nothing urgent to report. I intend to attend and return to the office at sixteen thirty.

The accounts appointment has revealed an administrative gap: the secretary has no ledgers or bills with them, and neither of us has established where the accounts are kept. I asked the secretary to locate existing records rather than invent figures. I am now beside the treasury chest to check for records; I have not yet inspected its contents. I cannot presently say whether any money is missing or any bills are outstanding.
